problemStatement: Provide an HTTP service that maps long URLs to short, unguessable codes, redirects code requests to the stored URL, and records per-link click counts by day, while preventing use as an attack vector (script URLs, internal-network targets, redirect loops) and limiting abuse.

functionalRequirements.text: POST /api/v1/links accepts a URL and returns a short code and short URL.
GET /{code} redirects to the stored URL.
GET /api/v1/links/{code}/stats returns total clicks and clicks per day.
Each redirect is counted without slowing the redirect.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Only http/https targets; reject javascript:, data:, credentials in URL, loopback/private IP literals and the service's own host.
Codes must not be enumerable (random, not sequential).
Creation is protected by per-client rate limiting.
Redirect p95 under 50 ms at the service boundary under nominal load.
Health and Prometheus metrics endpoints exposed.

acceptanceCriteria.then: 201 with code (7 Base62 chars), shortUrl and targetUrl
302 with Location equal to the stored URL

acceptanceCriteria.given: a javascript: URL or a 127.0.0.1 URL

ambiguities.question: Should links expire by default?
ambiguities.proposedDefault: No default expiry; clients may set expiresAt.
ambiguities.resolution: ASSUMED: No default expiry; clients may set expiresAt.

ambiguities.question: Should the same long URL always return the same code?
ambiguities.proposedDefault: No: each request creates a new code (simpler, per-campaign analytics).
ambiguities.resolution: ASSUMED: No: each request creates a new code (simpler, per-campaign analytics).

ambiguities.question: How long are click events retained?

assumptions: No user accounts in this increment; stats are readable by anyone who knows the code.
Single region deployment; in-memory rate limiting is acceptable for one instance.
